# One run per branch: a second push cancels the first build of that branch and leaves
# every other branch alone.
#
# `{pipeline}-{ref}` is the default, written out here to show what it expands to. Omit
# `concurrency` entirely and every push builds; set `cancel_in_progress: false` and it
# also builds, because queueing rather than cancelling is a separate behaviour Fiber does
# not yet have and will not guess at.
name: concurrency-demo
workspace:
  repo: https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git
  ref: master
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
concurrency:
  group: "{pipeline}-{ref}"
  cancel_in_progress: true

steps:
  checkout:
    run: test -f README && echo checked-out
    labels: [os=linux]

  slow-build:
    needs: [checkout]
    # Long enough that a second push lands while this is still running, which is the
    # whole point of the example.
    run: echo building && sleep 30 && echo built
    labels: [os=linux]

  publish:
    needs: [slow-build]
    run: echo publish
    labels: [os=linux]

name: nightly-cron
# Example: 6-field cron (with seconds). Fires at 02:00 UTC daily.
# Cron takes precedence over interval_minutes when both are set.
workspace:
  repo: https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git
  ref: master
on:
  cron: "0 0 2 * * *"
steps:
  checkout:
    run: ls -la
    labels: [os=linux]
  build:
    needs: [checkout]
    run: echo "nightly build"
    labels: [os=linux]

name: diamond-ci
workspace:
  repo: https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World.git
  ref: master
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
steps:
  checkout:
    run: ls -la && test -f README
    labels: [os=linux]
    retries: 1
  lint:
    needs: [checkout]
    run: echo linting && sleep 0.3
    labels: [os=linux]
  unit:
    name: unit tests
    needs: [checkout]
    run: echo unit && sleep 0.4
    labels: [os=linux]
    retries: 1
  types:
    name: typecheck
    needs: [checkout]
    run: echo typecheck && sleep 0.25
    labels: [os=linux]

# bindings. Values here are not secret — they live in the pipeline definition and are

    run: |
      echo "colour: $CARGO_TERM_COLOR"
      echo "log level: $RUST_LOG"
    labels: [os=linux]

  test:
    needs: [build]
    # Narrower than the pipeline's, for this step only.
    env:
      RUST_LOG: debug
      RUST_BACKTRACE: "1"
    run: |
      echo "log level: $RUST_LOG"      # debug, not info
      echo "backtrace: $RUST_BACKTRACE"
    labels: [os=linux]

  # A monorepo step: run somewhere else in the tree, under a different interpreter.
  # `artifacts` stays relative to the workspace root, not to working_directory.
  ui:
    needs: [build]
    working_directory: apps/ui
    shell: bash
    run: |
      echo "building in $PWD"

    labels: [os=linux]

# Fiber's own pipeline — the same gate CI runs, on a Fiber agent.
#
# Set it up once (see docs/triggers.md#dogfooding-this-repo):
#   fiber pipelines apply fiber.yml --project-id $PROJECT_ID
# then point a GitHub webhook with a secret at
#   https://<your fiber>/api/projects/$PROJECT_ID/webhooks/github
#
# Needs an agent labelled os=linux with Docker. Every step runs in a container, which is
# what makes building a pull request from a fork tolerable: that run gets no secrets and
# only a project-scoped agent will pick it up, but the container is what keeps it away
# from the agent's own environment. See docs/triggers.md#pull-requests-from-forks.
name: fiber
workspace:
  repo: https://github.com/durablefibers/fiber.git
  ref: main
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
timeout_minutes: 45

steps:
  fmt:
    run: cargo fmt --check
    image: rust:1.98-bookworm
    labels: [os=linux]
    timeout_minutes: 5
    secrets: []

  clippy:
    needs: [fmt]
    run: cargo clippy -p fiber-api -p fiber-agent -p fiber-cli -p fiber-core -p fiber-scheduler -p fiber-durable -- -D warnings
    image: rust:1.98-bookworm
    labels: [os=linux]
    timeout_minutes: 20
    secrets: []

  test:
    needs: [fmt]
    run: cargo test --workspace
    image: rust:1.98-bookworm
    labels: [os=linux]
    timeout_minutes: 20
    secrets: []

  build:
    needs: [clippy, test]
    run: cargo build --release -p fiber-api -p fiber-agent -p fiber-cli
    image: rust:1.98-bookworm
    labels: [os=linux]
    timeout_minutes: 25
    secrets: []

  ui:
    run: |
      cd apps/ui
      corepack enable
      pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      pnpm check
      pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
      pnpm test
      pnpm build
    image: node:22-bookworm
    labels: [os=linux]
    timeout_minutes: 15
    secrets: []
